answer: A harbor of agents can resist Sybils by making trust something you earn, not buy: each identity starts as a plain lotus seed with zero reputation and must complete weeks of verified, useful work before it can transact at full limits. Every completed job is chained to the agent history, and a single proven fraud burns that history to sable ash, non-transferable. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, because each one must still pay the same slow, real cost of work before it matters.
